# xshield_enforcement_snapshot (Data Source)

Fetches the AWS resources Xshield expects in one account and region, already rendered: each workload's own security group and rules, exactly as the cloud connector would write them, the interface attachments for instances, and a directory entry for each resource its own workspace attaches. Every map is keyed for `for_each`, by an instance ID or a handle such as `rds/orders-db`, so a plan names the workload each change is for.

Use it through the `aws` enforcement module, which creates these resources and reports the apply to Xshield.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Most configurations use this through the aws enforcement module, which
# creates every resource it lists. Reading it directly is useful for review:
# what would the next apply hold, and for which workloads?
data "xshield_enforcement_snapshot" "this" {
  cloud_account_id = "123456789012"
  region           = "us-east-1"
}

output "workloads" {
  value = sort(keys(data.xshield_enforcement_snapshot.this.security_groups))
}

output "rules_for_orders_db" {
  value = [for key, rule in data.xshield_enforcement_snapshot.this.ingress_rules : key if rule.security_group == "rds/orders-db"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cloud_account_id` (String) AWS account the snapshot is for.
- `region` (String) AWS region the snapshot is for.

### Optional

- `version` (Number) Pins a version, for break-glass rollback or forensics. When omitted, the version Xshield expects is fetched, so the configuration never changes when policy does. While a pin is in place, Xshield reports the account as pending.

### Read-Only

- `assets` (Map of Object) How each Xshield asset carries its group, keyed by Xshield asset ID. `security_group`: key, in `security_groups`, of the asset's group. Null when its policy holds no rule or was refused. `attached_by`: `pipeline` when this plan attaches it to the asset's interfaces, `owner` when the asset's own workspace does. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--assets))
- `content_hash` (String) Hash of everything this version asks for. Xshield accepts a receipt only for this exact content. Null when nothing is published.
- `directory` (Map of Object) One SSM parameter per database, function or service its own workspace attaches, keyed by handle. The `group-lookup` module reads it. An entry listing no group attaches nothing. `parameter_name`: `/colortokens/v1/<handle>/security-groups`. `handle`: the resource's kind and name, such as `rds/orders-db` or `lambda/orders-api`. `security_groups`: keys, in `security_groups`, of the groups the resource attaches. `tags`: tags for the parameter. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--directory))
- `egress_rules` (Map of Object) Every egress rule, one per source, keyed `<security group key>/<in|out>/<protocol>/<ports>/<source>`. A key encodes the rule's content, so a changed rule plans as one removal and one addition. Each value can be passed to `aws_vpc_security_group_egress_rule` as it is; attributes that do not apply are null. `security_group`: key, in `security_groups`, of the group the rule belongs to. `ip_protocol`: `tcp`, `udp`, `icmp`, `icmpv6`, `-1` for all traffic, or a protocol number. `from_port`, `to_port`: the port range, or the ICMP type and code (`-1` for all). Null for a protocol without ports. `cidr_ipv4`, `cidr_ipv6`, `prefix_list_id`, `referenced_security_group_id`: the source; exactly one is set. `referenced_security_group_id` is set only on a Full control cohort's copy of a customer rule that names a group. `description`, `tags`: the rule description and tags the cloud connector writes. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--egress_rules))
- `ingress_rules` (Map of Object) Every ingress rule, one per source, keyed `<security group key>/<in|out>/<protocol>/<ports>/<source>`. A key encodes the rule's content, so a changed rule plans as one removal and one addition. Each value can be passed to `aws_vpc_security_group_ingress_rule` as it is; attributes that do not apply are null. `security_group`: key, in `security_groups`, of the group the rule belongs to. `ip_protocol`: `tcp`, `udp`, `icmp`, `icmpv6`, `-1` for all traffic, or a protocol number. `from_port`, `to_port`: the port range, or the ICMP type and code (`-1` for all). Null for a protocol without ports. `cidr_ipv4`, `cidr_ipv6`, `prefix_list_id`, `referenced_security_group_id`: the source; exactly one is set. `referenced_security_group_id` is set only on a Full control cohort's copy of a customer rule that names a group. `description`, `tags`: the rule description and tags the cloud connector writes. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--ingress_rules))
- `published` (Boolean) False while Xshield has published nothing for this account and region, such as before the account is onboarded with policy delivery set to Terraform pipeline: every map is empty and `version` and `content_hash` are null, so a configuration built on it plans no change. Only Xshield's own answer that nothing is published counts; any other failure to read the snapshot fails the plan.
- `interface_attachments` (Map of Object) Each instance interface a group goes on, keyed `<security group key>/<interface ID>`. The attachment adds the group and leaves the interface's other groups in place, as the connector does. A contained instance's attachment is left out until the containment is reverted. `security_group`: key, in `security_groups`, of the group to attach. `network_interface_id`: interface to attach it to. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--interface_attachments))
- `security_groups` (Map of Object) One security group per workload, or per Aurora cluster, keyed by its instance ID or handle, and at Full control one `ct-cohort-` group per cohort, keyed by its name, for the workloads that keep a rule their customer group gives up. `name`, `description`: fixed for the group's life, named as the cloud connector names its groups. `vpc_id`: VPC the group is created in. `tags`: let the cloud connector recognise the group as Xshield's, never as a customer group. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--security_groups))
- `withdrawing` (List of String) Keys of groups policy no longer uses but a resource may still carry. They keep their rules until Xshield sees them detached, because AWS refuses to delete an attached group.
